section_1.title: Prerequisites: The Language of Flux
section_1.content: Establish the Reynolds Number (Re) as the dimensionless ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces. Explain that turbulence emerges when Re exceeds a critical threshold, leading to energy cascade.
section_1.example: Visualizing a 'Honey vs. Water' experiment: Honey (low Re) flows in smooth layers; water (high Re) breaks into chaotic eddies.

section_2.title: The Kolmogorov Hypothesis: Self-Similarity
section_2.content: Introduce Kolmogorov’s 1941 theory (K41). Explain the 'Energy Cascade' where large eddies break into smaller ones until viscous dissipation dominates. Define the Kolmogorov length scale (η) and time scale (τ).
section_2.example: An animation of a large 'Whirlpool' splitting into smaller circles, showing that statistics are the same regardless of scale (fractal-like behavior).

section_3.title: The Mathematical Structure: The 5/3 Law
section_3.content: Derive the Power Spectrum E(k) ~ C * ε^(2/3) * k^(-5/3). Define ε (dissipation rate) and C (Kolmogorov constant, ~1.5). Focus on the 'inertial subrange' where viscosity is negligible.
section_3.example: A graph plotting log(Energy) vs log(Wavenumber). Show a distinct '-5/3' slope line superimposed over the curve of a turbulent smoke plume.

section_4.title: Application: Turbulence in Nature
section_4.content: Connect the math to real-world energy distribution. Discuss why this statistical predictability matters for aerodynamics and climate modeling.
section_4.example: A 'Peregrine Falcon' diving: The bird manages turbulent air pockets by utilizing the energy cascade to stabilize its trajectory at high velocities.

section_5.title: Summary and Conclusion
section_5.content: Recap: Turbulence is not truly random; it follows statistical laws dictated by the constant C and the energy dissipation rate ε. The -5/3 law is the 'DNA' of turbulent flow.
section_5.example: A quick visual loop summarizing the scale transition from macro (large eddies) to micro (dissipation) as a final 'big picture' slide.
